title: Aura and Visualforce recognition, interoperability, and migration decisions
objectives: Recognize Aura versus Visualforce versus LWC from markup, folders, and runtime containers.
State the coexistence rule: Aura may contain LWC; LWC may not contain Aura.
Decide what to migrate by usage and facets, not by rewriting every working page.
Know that Lightning Out and Visualforce do not get lightning/navigation and other LEX-only modules.
diagnostic_question: A record page mixes an Aura wrapper, an LWC child, and a Visualforce iframe. What can contain what, what should you migrate first, and which navigation APIs will silently fail?
definition: Aura and Visualforce recognition, interoperability, and migration decisions are how you identify the three UI stacks, compose them legally, and choose what to rewrite. Aura and LWC coexist in the same Lightning runtime: an Aura component can contain a Lightning web component; a Lightning web component cannot contain an Aura component. If an Aura component’s facets contain other Aura components, those must migrate too. Visualforce is a different container; Lightning Out and Lightning Components for Visualforce do not support lightning/navigation. ([Pick a Component to Migrate](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/migrate-decide.html); [Migrate Aura Components](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/migrate-introduction.html); [Navigate to Pages](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/use-navigate.html))
why_it_matters: Interviewers fail 'rewrite everything in LWC this sprint' and 'drop Aura inside LWC.' Facets create hidden Aura children. Visualforce plus Lightning Out looks like LWC but loses navigation and some toasts. Recognition from file names (.cmp vs .js/.html vs .page) is the first 30 seconds of the answer.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a mixed rail fleet on one campus. Visualforce is the heritage streetcar on its own rails. Aura is the older locomotive that can still couple a new LWC passenger car. LWC is the new electric multiple unit: it cannot swallow an Aura locomotive inside itself. Interoperability is legal coupling. Migration is retiring a locomotive when the route and the coupled cars are ready—not scrapping the whole yard because one new car arrived.
deeper_explanation: Recognition: Visualforce uses .page/.component and Apex controllers, often Classic or VF tabs. Aura uses .cmp/.auradoc in aura/ folders and aura: attributes. LWC uses lwc/ folders with HTML, JS, CSS, js-meta.xml. Lightning App Builder may host Aura and LWC side by side on a record page.

Interoperability: Aura and LWC share the Lightning runtime. Aura can contain LWC. LWC cannot contain Aura. Facets in Aura that hold nested Aura force those nested pieces onto the migration path too. Events and data-binding differ; the migrate guide has dedicated pages for markup, events, CSS, and Apex. ([Pick a Component to Migrate](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/migrate-decide.html))

Visualforce interoperability is usually Lightning Components for Visualforce or Lightning Out / Lightning Out 2.0—not nesting VF inside LWC as a first-class child. Those containers do not support lightning/navigation even when they appear inside Lightning Experience. Plan URL changes accordingly (LWC-008).

Migration decisions: new work prefers LWC. Migrate an Aura component when you must change it, when you need LWC-only APIs, or when the wrapper exists only to host LWC. Do not migrate a stable Aura that you never touch just for fashion. Understand facets before you pick a leaf. Use the official Aura-to-LWC mapping topics rather than inventing a one-to-one API cheat sheet from memory.
LWS applies to Aura and LWC (GA Summer ’23). A Visualforce page is not 'fixed' by LWS. Tests: Jest for LWC (LWC-012), not Aura test suites.

mental_model.analogy: A mixed rail fleet: Visualforce streetcar on separate rails, Aura locomotive that can couple an LWC car, LWC train that cannot swallow an Aura locomotive.
useful_mapping: streetcar rails → Visualforce / Classic VF container
Aura locomotive → .cmp component that may wrap LWC
LWC passenger car → modern component, cannot contain Aura
coupled cars that must all convert → Aura facets of nested Aura
missing corridor on the streetcar line → no lightning/navigation in Lightning Out
scrapping the yard overnight → unjustified big-bang migration
where_it_breaks: A real railroad can rebuild a locomotive around a car; LWC still cannot host Aura.
Lightning App Builder can place Aura and LWC as siblings without nesting.
Managed-package Aura may be unmigratable even if the analogy says 'retire it.'

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: I recognize VF, Aura, and LWC from files. Aura may wrap LWC; LWC never wraps Aura. Facets pull nested Aura into the migration. Visualforce/Out loses lightning/navigation. I migrate by usage, not fashion.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: New work is LWC. A stable Aura wrapper can host a new LWC child. If I touch the Aura parent, I map facets first. I do not promise NavigationMixin inside Lightning Out. I do not big-bang the org. LWS applies to Aura and LWC, not as a VF rewrite.

terminology.plain: The older Lightning component model using .cmp markup.
terminology.precise: Lives in the Lightning runtime with LWC. May contain LWC. Cannot be nested inside LWC. Facets can hide more Aura children.
terminology.example: aura:component wrapping c:labKpiTile LWC on a record page.
terminology.boundary: Aura events and value binding differ; see migrate-events.

terminology.plain: The page-centric UI framework that predates Lightning.
terminology.precise: Recognized by .page and Apex controllers. Embedding LWC typically uses Lightning Out or Lightning Components for Visualforce, which lack lightning/navigation.
terminology.example: A VF console page hosting Lightning Out.
terminology.non_example: A Lightning record page with only LWC.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent a VF-inside-LWC first-class tag.

terminology.plain: Legal ways the stacks share a screen.
terminology.precise: Aura hosts LWC. Sibling placement on App Builder. VF hosts via Out. Not LWC hosts Aura.
terminology.example: Aura parent, LWC child, both on one LEX page.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lightning Message Service across stacks (neighboring communication topic).

terminology.plain: Rewriting Aura (or VF) UI into LWC when it is justified.
terminology.precise: Evaluate how and where the component is used. Migrate nested Aura in facets together. Prefer LWC for new work. Mapping guides exist for markup, events, CSS, Apex, quick actions.
terminology.example: Rewriting an Aura quick action you must change into an LWC screen action (LWC-008).
terminology.non_example: Rewriting a untouched managed Aura header this sprint.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Lift-and-shift of Visualforce with no container analysis.
terminology.boundary: Do not memorize unofficial API maps; open the migrate-* pages.

terminology.plain: An Aura region that can hold other components as children.
terminology.precise: If those children are Aura, they are on the migration hook: you must migrate them too when you migrate the parent.
terminology.example: An Aura layout facet that includes another Aura filter bar.
terminology.boundary: Understand facets before picking a leaf component.

terminology.plain: Telling VF, Aura, and LWC apart in an org or a repo.
terminology.precise: Folders (pages, aura, lwc), file suffixes, and which builder opened the source. Interviewers start here.
terminology.example: Seeing aura:iteration versus lwc:if in a screenshot.
terminology.non_example: Guessing from the business object name alone.

when_to_use: When you must recognize Aura versus Visualforce versus LWC and decide interoperability or migration.
When an Aura wrapper should host a new LWC instead of a forbidden LWC-contains-Aura design.
When Aura facets contain nested Aura that would be stranded by a parent-only rewrite.
When a Visualforce or Lightning Out host cannot use lightning/navigation and the migration plan must account for that.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this migration lesson as a mandate to rewrite every stable Aura or Visualforce page this quarter.
Do not nest Aura inside LWC, or assume Lightning Out has the same navigation and toast modules as LEX.
Do not skip facet inventory, or treat LWS as a Visualforce rewrite.
Do not invent one-to-one Aura-to-LWC API maps from memory; open the official migrate topics.

decision_table.signal: Need a new widget on an existing Aura record header.
decision_table.choose: Build LWC and let Aura contain it, or place LWC as an App Builder sibling.
decision_table.not: An LWC parent that tries to include the Aura header.
decision_table.why: Aura can contain LWC; LWC cannot contain Aura.

decision_table.signal: You must change an Aura parent whose facets include other Aura components.
decision_table.choose: Inventory and migrate those nested Aura pieces in the same plan.
decision_table.not: Rewrite only the parent and leave Aura children in facets.
decision_table.why: The migrate-decide topic says those other Aura components must migrate too.

decision_table.signal: The UI is Visualforce or Lightning Out and must open a record page like LEX.
decision_table.choose: Redesign navigation; do not use lightning/navigation in that container.
decision_table.not: Copy NavigationMixin from the Lightning Experience LWC.
decision_table.why: The Navigate topic lists VF Lightning components and Lightning Out as unsupported.

decision_table.signal: An Aura component is stable, unused in the current project, and not blocking LWC.
decision_table.choose: Leave it; put new work in LWC beside it.
decision_table.not: A fashion-driven big-bang rewrite this sprint.
decision_table.why: Pick a component to migrate by how and where it is used.

interview_questions.question: Explain Aura and Visualforce recognition, interoperability, and migration decisions.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: I identify VF, Aura, and LWC from files. Aura may wrap LWC; LWC never wraps Aura. Facets pull nested Aura along. Out/VF lose lightning/navigation. I migrate by usage.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: New work is LWC. A stable Aura parent is a legal host. I inventory facets before promising a rewrite. I treat Visualforce as another container, not 'old Aura.' I refuse big-bang fashion migrations and illegal nesting in the same breath.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Account: Aura header hosts labKpiTile; VF console path has no NavigationMixin.
weak_answer_warnings: Rewrite everything in LWC this sprint

interview_questions.question: What is the coexistence nesting rule?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Same Lightning runtime. Aura can contain LWC. LWC cannot contain Aura.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw the arrow only one way. Siblings on App Builder are fine. Facets are how extra Aura sneaks into a parent migration. Interviewers listen for the negative sentence: LWC cannot contain Aura.
interview_questions.example: On a whiteboard I draw Aura wrapping LWC as legal, and LWC wrapping Aura as illegal.
tradeoffs: Wrapper Aura forever versus full LWC page

interview_questions.question: You migrate an Aura layout and the filter bar disappears. What happened?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A facet still expected an Aura child you did not migrate. Nested Aura must come along.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I go back to migrate-decide. I list facets before coding. I either migrate the filter Aura to LWC or keep the parent Aura until the children are ready. I do not blame App Builder visibility first.
interview_questions.example: Aura facet body included c:labFilterBar Aura; parent became LWC with an empty slot.
tradeoffs: Migrate children first versus keep parent Aura

interview_questions.question: A VF page hosts your LWC through Lightning Out. Product copies LEX navigation code. Your review?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Reject lightning/navigation. That container is unsupported even inside LEX chrome.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I separate LEX record-page builds from Out builds. I offer a VF-safe URL or keep navigation in VF. I also re-check toasts (LWC-008). This is recognition of container, not a PageReference typo.
tradeoffs: Stay on a Lightning page versus VF
Two codepaths versus one limited path
weak_answer_warnings: It is inside LEX so navigation works

interview_questions.question: A developer pastes an Aura component tag into LWC HTML. What do you tell them?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: That composition is invalid. Host the LWC from Aura or place them as siblings.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show the migrate-decide bullets. I help them invert the parent. I do not hunt for a namespace prefix as if that would legalize Aura-in-LWC. If they need slots, those are LWC children, still not Aura.
interview_questions.example: Failed compile or runtime when c:oldAura sat in labNew.html.
tradeoffs: App Builder siblings versus code nesting
weak_answer_warnings: Add a namespace and it will work

interview_questions.question: How do you recognize which stack owns a buggy widget in a mixed page?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Inspect DOM/file path: lwc-* custom elements, Aura rendered markup, or a VF iframe/Out root. Then open the matching folder.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not guess from the business name. I use Setup Custom Code lists and the repo. Mixed pages lie; the header can be Aura while the body is LWC. Recognition is step one of troubleshooting.
interview_questions.example: Chrome inspect shows c-lab-kpi-tile versus an Aura namespace element.
follow_ups: What if it is a managed Aura?
weak_answer_warnings: It is all Lightning so it is LWC

interview_questions.question: When do you refuse a full Aura-to-LWC migration project?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the Aura is stable, unused this quarter, managed-locked, or the real need is a small LWC beside it. Facet cost can also exceed benefit.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I still prefer LWC for new work. I will not burn a team on fashion rewrites. I quantify nested Aura, VF/Out hosts, and test debt (Jest versus Aura tests). I propose hosting first, migrate when we must change the parent.
interview_questions.example: Leaving a managed console Aura; adding labKpiTile via App Builder.

interview_questions.question: Teach nesting and VF with a rail-fleet analogy, then break it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: VF is a streetcar on other rails. Aura can couple an LWC car. LWC cannot swallow an Aura locomotive. The break: App Builder can park them as siblings without coupling, and managed locomotives may never be scrapped.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I also break navigation: the streetcar line has no LEX corridor, so lightning/navigation fails in Out. Facets are extra cars already coupled that you forgot to count. I never use a library metaphor.
interview_questions.example: Whiteboard three tracks and one illegal arrow.
